title: Geographic entitlement decision flow for enterprise requests
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: Enterprise customers increasingly request either new geographic presence (new region enablement) or strict data residency guarantees and failover behaviors. Current intake is informal and inconsistent across sales, CSM, and security which causes long lead times and missed contractual SLAs. Goal: Define a reproducible decision flow and scoring rubric (entitlement gate) that product, sales, and engineering can use to triage, prioritize, and accept/reject region/residency requests. Scope: non-bug feature triage for region availability, residency constraints, and runbook-level failover requirements (does not include full procurement or datacenter contract negotiations). Out of scope: ad-hoc support for single-customer manual deployments where a contract and Dedicated/Private plan already exist.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable entitlement decision flow (flowchart + checklist) published in Confluence
A scoring rubric with weighted criteria that produces a numeric priority score for each request
Stakeholder matrix (who owns intake, compliance review, infra feasibility, cost estimation) published
Pilot triage of 3 backlog requests using the flow with documented outcomes and time-to-decision measured
Onboarding owners (Sales/CS/PM/Infra/Security) agree to SLA: initial decision within 10 business days for complete requests
decision_rubric: Mandatory residency: boolean (weight 30) — Is customer contractually required to keep data within a jurisdiction? (yes = high priority)
Market strategic value: score 0-10 (weight 20) — Is this a high motion account or opens an entire vertical/region?
Failure-domain risk: score 0-10 (weight 15) — Does enabling this region materially improve global failover/resilience for other customers?
Operational cost delta: qualitative (weight 15) — Estimated incremental monthly cost to Redwood (GPU/infra/ops). Convert to score bracket (low/med/high).
Time-to-prod estimate: days (weight 10) — Engineering ETA to enable region with current infra automation. Shorter ETA increases priority.
Security/compliance friction: score 0-10 (weight 10) — Additional controls required (KMS, audit, penetration tests, cross-border transfer mitigations).

proposed_timeline: Week 0: Draft flow + rubric (this ticket) — PM builds draft and solicits stakeholder feedback
Week 1: Alignment workshops with Infra, Security, Sales, CS — validate feasibility bands and cost buckets
Week 2: Publish Confluence decision flow and create an intake template (structured form)
Week 3-4: Run pilot on 3 historic/active requests, collect metrics (time-to-decision, score distribution, stakeholder effort)
Week 5: Iterate rubric and put intake form into standard playbook; roll out to Sales/CS
Week 6: Automate scoring into Linear intake (optional follow-up ticket: ENG-automation)
